content.text: No exclusivity obligation binding Corio exists anywhere in the agreement. Submitting a compliant finding.

input.quote: 2.1 Hosting Software License. Subject to the terms and conditions of this Agreement, Commerce One hereby grants to Corio a fee-bearing, perpetual and irrevocable, nonexclusive, nontransferable (except in accordance with Section 14.1 of this Agreement), right and license in the Territory to (i) reproduce the Software in machine executable object code format only for installation on the Corio Servers;
input.rationale: The agreement imposes no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation on Corio (our party). All licences in Section 2 are expressly "nonexclusive" and run in our favour; Section 2.7 restricts only copying/reverse engineering of the Software, not our freedom to source competing procurement or hosting software from third parties. Section 2.4 in fact operates in our favour by barring Commerce One from contacting Corio Customers for non-ASP licence sales and requiring referrals to us. Section 13 (Shared Resources) and the CORIO MARKET SEGMENT definition (Section 1.3) limit customer segment and territory scope but contain no requirements/exclusive-dealing covenant, and Exhibit D sales and marketing cooperation is expressly stated to be "non-binding" (p0198), so the cross-selling and joint marketing commitments create no enforceable soft exclusivity. This meets the preferred position (no exclusivity obligation on the customer); no redline needed.
